Prepare the Distribution Form content and testing instructions

approval.cost: No fee mentioned anywhere in the publishing docs (unverified)
approval.trigger: Depends on flavor. Classic User OAuth: no review; 'a user on any account can authorize it as soon as it is registered, without publishing' (publishing is optional, for discovery in PagerDuty's integrations library). Scoped OAuth: publishing review is required before it works on any account other than the one that created it; until published it 'behaves as a private app: it only works on the account that created it'. To publish: set App Type to Public, complete the Distribution Form (listing information: documentation, support contact, plus instructions for testing your app), Save, Save on Edit App, confirm submission; you get a confirmation email. During review PagerDuty tests the app's functionality, reviews documentation for completeness and accuracy, and verifies listing information; reviewers may request changes by email (apps@pagerduty.com). Second gate after approval: before any user on a customer account can authorize a published Scoped OAuth app, an admin on that account must install it (via app.pagerduty.com/oauth_apps/[app_id]); installing grants no access by itself, each user still completes the OAuth flow, and until installed, authorization attempts from that account fail.
approval.wait: 'We aim to review your submission and approve or reply with feedback within 5 business days' (stated)

blockers.detail: 'The authorization code is valid for 30 seconds' and the token POST 'must be received within that time'. Slow callbacks and clock skew will fail exchanges.
blockers.howToClear: Exchange the code immediately in the callback handler; no queuing or retries with the same code.
blockers.title: 30-second authorization codes

blockers.detail: If you request an invalid scope, PagerDuty returns NO error; it grants partial scopes, only the openid scope automatically attached to all tokens. You must inspect the scope field of the token response to detect that your app got almost nothing.
blockers.howToClear: Validate the returned scope set on every token response and fail loudly in your logs/UI.
blockers.title: Invalid scopes fail silently

blockers.detail: 'Once you submit, you will no longer be able to make updates to your app.' Getting it back into an editable draft requires emailing apps@pagerduty.com.
blockers.howToClear: Freeze configuration before submitting; treat submission as a release.
blockers.title: Submission freezes the app

blockers.detail: The client-credentials (app token) flow 'only works on the account that created the app'. On customer accounts you get user tokens only, so app-level automation across customers is not available.
blockers.howToClear: Design for per-user tokens on customer accounts; use app tokens only on your own account.
blockers.title: Scoped app tokens don't travel

Any user/install cap before approval, and any limit on number of apps per account.
Whether redirect URIs are limited in count / multiple redirect URIs supported (docs speak of 'the Redirect URL').

Per-app rate limits for the OAuth endpoints themselves.

alternatives: Classic User OAuth (legacy: authorization code grant acting as a user, single blanket scope read or write, case-sensitive; works on any account the moment it is registered with no publishing; the only flavor that supports non-confidential browser/mobile clients)
flavor.recommended: A PagerDuty App with Scoped OAuth and user tokens (authorization code grant)
flavor.why: An app is a container created via App Registration (My Apps); you add OAuth 2.0 functionality and choose the flavor at that moment. Scoped OAuth gives per-resource-type scopes (incidents.read, services.read; every REST endpoint documents its required scope) and is the only least-privilege option. Scoped OAuth apps are always confidential clients: the client_secret must be sent on the token request AND PKCE is mandatory. Effective access is always the intersection of the app's granted scopes and the authorizing user's own permissions.

humanMust: Hold a Manager, Global Admin, or Account Owner base role (App Registration is not available below Manager)
Register the app and choose the OAuth flavor in the UI; custody the client_secret
For Scoped distribution: set App Type to Public, complete the Distribution Form, and submit
Each customer account's admin must install the published app before its users can authorize
name: PagerDuty
nuances: Token lifetimes differ sharply by flavor (stated): Classic access token 30 days, refresh 210 days, rolling window 3 years (activity at least once every 210 days). Scoped access token 1 day, refresh 30 days, rolling window 1 year (use at least once every 30 days). Refresh tokens apply to user tokens only; expired app tokens are simply re-requested.

Apps are immovable: 'Apps are associated with a PagerDuty subdomain and a user and cannot be moved between subdomains or users. Continued access to this subdomain and user is needed to make any configuration changes.' Losing that user or subdomain orphans the app configuration.
Deleting OAuth functionality does NOT revoke tokens: use 'Revoke All Tokens' on the OAuth Client screen before deleting the functionality, or outstanding tokens survive.
App Type does not apply to Classic User OAuth: Classic works cross-account regardless; 'Private' app type only constrains Scoped OAuth (and Events) apps.
A 403 can mean the token lacks the endpoint's scope OR the endpoint does not yet support API scopes; a 401 means the token expired and a new one must be obtained.
prerequisites: A PagerDuty developer account, or a customer account with base role Manager, Global Admin, or Account Owner
A redirect URL registered with the app (the runtime redirect_uri must match it)
For publishing: listing information (documentation, support contact) and instructions for testing your app

steps.detail: App Registration requires a developer account or a customer account where your base role is Manager, Global Admin, or Account Owner.
steps.title: Get access to App Registration

steps.detail: Integrations > Developer Tools > App Registration > My Apps > New App; enter name and brief description in the wizard. No app-registration API is documented.
steps.title: Register the app

steps.detail: On the Edit App page, Functionality section, Add on the OAuth card; on the Configure OAuth 2.0 screen choose Classic User OAuth or Scoped OAuth. Configure the redirect URL and permission scopes. Saving generates the client_id and client_secret.
steps.title: Add OAuth functionality (choose the flavor)

steps.detail: Authorize at identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/authorize (response_type=code, scope, PKCE code_challenge S256: always for Scoped, recommended for Classic); exchange at identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/token with client_secret and code_verifier, within 30 seconds of the code being issued. Store access + refresh tokens and implement refresh. Inspect the returned scope field: invalid requested scopes fail silently down to openid only.
steps.title: Implement the flow

steps.detail: Classic works cross-account immediately. For Scoped on other accounts: set App Type to Public, complete the Distribution Form with testing instructions, submit (the app freezes for edits on submission), and wait for review ('within 5 business days' to approve or reply). After approval, an admin on each customer account must install the app before its users can authorize.
steps.title: (Scoped, distributing) Publish and get installed

tagline: A two-flavor system with opposite trade-offs: the least-privilege flavor (Scoped OAuth) works only on your own account until it passes a publishing review (reply within 5 business days) and an admin installs it on every customer account, while the ungated flavor (Classic) forces blanket read or write access everywhere.

time.active: ~15 min of app setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day for Classic or own-account Scoped; add up to 5 business days of review (stated) plus per-account admin installs for Scoped distribution
time.waiting: Publishing review: within 5 business days to approve or reply (stated)
